Looking at this problem, I need to determine whether the set of weak MSO sentences valid over all finite linear orders under Henkin semantics is recursively axiomatizable.

**Answer: Yes, an axiomatization exists.**

## Proof

The proof has two key steps: (1) Henkin semantics collapses to full semantics for finite linear orders, and (2) the resulting (full-semantics) theory is decidable, hence recursively axiomatizable.

### Step 1: Henkin Semantics = Full Semantics for Finite Linear Orders

**Definition.** A Henkin (general) model for monadic second-order logic over a structure $(L, <)$ is a triple $(L, <, \mathcal{F})$ where $\mathcal{F} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(L)$ is closed under MSO-definability: for every MSO formula $\varphi(x, \bar{Z})$ and every $\bar{S} \in \mathcal{F}^{|Z|}$, the set $\{a \in L : (L, <, \mathcal{F}) \models \varphi(a, \bar{S})\}$ belongs to $\mathcal{F}$.

**Claim.** For every finite linear order $L_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ with the usual order, and every Henkin model $(L_n, <, \mathcal{F})$, we have $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{P}(L_n)$.

**Proof of Claim.** It suffices to show every subset $S \subseteq L_n$ is parameter-free first-order definable, since comprehension (even parameter-free) then forces $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

For each $k \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, define the first-order formula $\text{pos}_k(x)$ meaning "$x$ is the $k$-th element" (i.e., exactly $k$ elements are strictly below $x$):

$$\text{pos}_k(x) := \exists y_1 \cdots \exists y_k \left[\bigwedge_{i \neq j} y_i \neq y_j \wedge \bigwedge_i y_i < x \wedge \forall z (z < x \rightarrow \bigvee_i z = y_i)\right]$$

This is a parameter-free FO formula. For any $S \subseteq L_n$, the formula:

$$\psi_S(x) := \bigvee_{k \in S} \text{pos}_k(x)$$

is a parameter-free FO (hence MSO) formula defining exactly $S$. By the comprehension closure of $\mathcal{F}$, we have $S \in \mathcal{F}$. Since $S$ was arbitrary, $\mathcal{P}(L_n) \subseteq \mathcal{F}$, and since $\mathcal{F} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(L_n)$ trivially, we conclude $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{P}(L_n)$. $\square$

**Corollary.** Every Henkin model over a finite linear order is the full model. Therefore, the weak MSO theory of finite linear orders under Henkin semantics is identical to the (weak) MSO theory under full semantics. (The "weak" qualifier is moot here since every subset of a finite set is finite, so weak MSO = MSO over finite structures.)

### Step 2: The MSO Theory of Finite Linear Orders Is Decidable

By the **Büchi–Elgot–Trakhtenbrot theorem**, there is an effective translation from any MSO sentence $\varphi$ over the signature $\{<\}$ to a finite automaton $\mathcal{A}_\varphi$ such that:

$$\varphi \text{ is satisfiable over some finite linear order} \iff L(\mathcal{A}_\varphi) \neq \emptyset$$

Since emptiness of finite automata is decidable, satisfiability of MSO over finite linear orders is decidable. Validity (truth in *all* finite linear orders) is the complement: $\varphi$ is valid iff $\neg\varphi$ is not satisfiable. Hence validity is also decidable.

### Step 3: Decidable ⟹ Recursively Axiomatizable

The weak MSO theory of finite linear orders under Henkin semantics — call it $T$ — is the set of MSO sentences true in all finite linear orders under Henkin semantics. By Step 1, this equals the set of sentences true in all finite linear orders under full semantics. By Step 2, $T$ is decidable.

A decidable theory is recursively enumerable: enumerate all sentences $\varphi_1, \varphi_2, \dots$ and, for each, decide whether $\varphi_i \in T$. The set $T$ itself serves as a recursive set of axioms (every element of $T$ is an axiom, and the inference rules are just modus ponens or trivial). Equivalently, since $T$ is decidable, it is r.e., and every r.e. theory has a recursive axiomatization (by a standard result in computability theory: an r.e. set is the set of theorems of some recursive axiom system).

### Conclusion

An axiomatization exists for the weak monadic second-order theory of finite linear orders under Henkin semantics. The key insight is that over finite linear orders, every subset is parameter-free first-order definable (by specifying positions in the order), which forces every Henkin general model to be the full power-set model. This collapses Henkin semantics to full semantics, and the resulting theory is decidable by the Büchi–Elgot–Trakhtenbrot theorem, hence recursively axiomatizable.

## Proof

The proof has two key steps: (1) Henkin semantics collapses to full semantics for finite linear orders, and (2) the resulting (full-semantics) theory is decidable, hence recursively axiomatizable.

### Step 1: Henkin Semantics = Full Semantics for Finite Linear Orders

**Definition.** A Henkin (general) model for monadic second-order logic over a structure $(L, <)$ is a triple $(L, <, \mathcal{F})$ where $\mathcal{F} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(L)$ is closed under MSO-definability: for every MSO formula $\varphi(x, \bar{Z})$ and every $\bar{S} \in \mathcal{F}^{|Z|}$, the set $\{a \in L : (L, <, \mathcal{F}) \models \varphi(a, \bar{S})\}$ belongs to $\mathcal{F}$.

**Claim.** For every finite linear order $L_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ with the usual order, and every Henkin model $(L_n, <, \mathcal{F})$, we have $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{P}(L_n)$.

**Proof of Claim.** It suffices to show every subset $S \subseteq L_n$ is parameter-free first-order definable, since comprehension (even parameter-free) then forces $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

For each $k \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, define the first-order formula $\text{pos}_k(x)$ meaning "$x$ is the $k$-th element" (i.e., exactly $k$ elements are strictly below $x$):

$$\text{pos}_k(x) := \exists y_1 \cdots \exists y_k \left[\bigwedge_{i \neq j} y_i \neq y_j \wedge \bigwedge_i y_i < x \wedge \forall z (z < x \rightarrow \bigvee_i z = y_i)\right]$$

This is a parameter-free FO formula. For any $S \subseteq L_n$, the formula:

$$\psi_S(x) := \bigvee_{k \in S} \text{pos}_k(x)$$

is a parameter-free FO (hence MSO) formula defining exactly $S$. By the comprehension closure of $\mathcal{F}$, we have $S \in \mathcal{F}$. Since $S$ was arbitrary, $\mathcal{P}(L_n) \subseteq \mathcal{F}$, and since $\mathcal{F} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(L_n)$ trivially, we conclude $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{P}(L_n)$. $\square$

**Corollary.** Every Henkin model over a finite linear order is the full model. Therefore, the weak MSO theory of finite linear orders under Henkin semantics is identical to the (weak) MSO theory under full semantics. (The "weak" qualifier is moot here since every subset of a finite set is finite, so weak MSO = MSO over finite structures.)

### Step 2: The MSO Theory of Finite Linear Orders Is Decidable

By the **Büchi–Elgot–Trakhtenbrot theorem**, there is an effective translation from any MSO sentence $\varphi$ over the signature $\{<\}$ to a finite automaton $\mathcal{A}_\varphi$ such that:

$$\varphi \text{ is satisfiable over some finite linear order} \iff L(\mathcal{A}_\varphi) \neq \emptyset$$

Since emptiness of finite automata is decidable, satisfiability of MSO over finite linear orders is decidable. Validity (truth in *all* finite linear orders) is the complement: $\varphi$ is valid iff $\neg\varphi$ is not satisfiable. Hence validity is also decidable.

### Step 3: Decidable ⟹ Recursively Axiomatizable

The weak MSO theory of finite linear orders under Henkin semantics — call it $T$ — is the set of MSO sentences true in all finite linear orders under Henkin semantics. By Step 1, this equals the set of sentences true in all finite linear orders under full semantics. By Step 2, $T$ is decidable.

A decidable theory is recursively enumerable: enumerate all sentences $\varphi_1, \varphi_2, \dots$ and, for each, decide whether $\varphi_i \in T$. The set $T$ itself serves as a recursive set of axioms (every element of $T$ is an axiom, and the inference rules are just modus ponens or trivial). Equivalently, since $T$ is decidable, it is r.e., and every r.e. theory has a recursive axiomatization (by a standard result in computability theory: an r.e. set is the set of theorems of some recursive axiom system).

### Conclusion

An axiomatization exists for the weak monadic second-order theory of finite linear orders under Henkin semantics. The key insight is that over finite linear orders, every subset is parameter-free first-order definable (by specifying positions in the order), which forces every Henkin general model to be the full power-set model. This collapses Henkin semantics to full semantics, and the resulting theory is decidable by the Büchi–Elgot–Trakhtenbrot theorem, hence recursively axiomatizable.
